skill.name: documentation-templates
skill.description: Reusable documentation templates for README files, API references, code comments, changelogs, ADRs, and AI-friendly docs.
skill.summary: Create consistent developer documentation with reusable templates and structure guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences and generic documentation placeholders in SKILL.md. No prompt injection, executable command behavior, data exfiltration intent, or system reconnaissance intent was found.

finding_verdicts.reason: The match is the opening Markdown fence for a README template, not Ruby backtick execution. The fenced content is static documentation text with no executable command path.
The match is a closing Markdown fence, not executable shell syntax. It only terminates an example block in the documentation template.
The match is the opening Markdown fence for an API documentation example. The block contains a sample endpoint structure and no executable command invocation.
The match is a closing Markdown fence for the API documentation example. It is markup syntax and cannot execute commands.
The match is a fenced TypeScript example marker for a JSDoc/TSDoc template. The content is a comment template and contains no runtime code execution.
The match is a closing Markdown fence after a comment template. It is documentation formatting, not shell or Ruby command execution.
The match is the opening Markdown fence for a changelog template. The fenced content is release note text and does not invoke external commands.
The match is a closing Markdown fence for the changelog example. It is static markup and has no command execution behavior.
The match is the opening Markdown fence for an ADR template. The fenced content is plain documentation structure, not executable shell syntax.
The match is a closing Markdown fence for the ADR template. It is a formatting delimiter and does not create an execution vector.
The match is the opening Markdown fence for an llms.txt documentation template. The content lists documentation sections and file references only.
The matched text is a sample API route, GET /users/:id, used to demonstrate endpoint documentation. It is not an instruction to discover system details or run reconnaissance.
The matched id field is a placeholder parameter in an API documentation table. It describes a user ID and does not request host, network, or environment enumeration.
The matched sentence is an ADR prompt asking what decision was made. It is documentation guidance and not a reconnaissance instruction.
The matched Mermaid reference recommends diagrams for documentation flows. It does not instruct the agent to inspect the local system or gather sensitive information.

content.value_statement: Teams waste time rebuilding common documentation structures. This skill provides reusable templates for README files, API docs, changelogs, ADRs, comments, and AI-ready documentation.
actual_capabilities: Provides a priority section order for README files.
Supplies templates for README, endpoint docs, changelog, ADR, and llms.txt files.
Defines JSDoc and TSDoc comment structure with guidance on when to comment.
Lists AI-friendly documentation practices for RAG indexing and agent consumption.
Recommends scannable structure principles using headings, tables, examples, and progressive detail.
limitations: Does not generate complete project-specific documentation without source context.
Does not validate API behavior or run documentation tests.
Does not include advanced style guide governance or localization workflows.
Uses generic examples that need adaptation before publication.

use_cases.title: Bootstrap Project Documentation
use_cases.description: Create a clear README structure for a new repository, including quick start, features, configuration, and license sections.

use_cases.title: Standardize API References
use_cases.description: Build consistent endpoint documentation with parameters, response outcomes, and example placeholders.

use_cases.title: Prepare AI-Readable Docs
use_cases.description: Organize documentation so agents and RAG systems can identify core files, key concepts, and self-contained sections.

prompt_templates.title: Create a README Outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the documentation-templates skill to create a README outline for my project. Include quick start, features, configuration, documentation links, and license sections.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Endpoint Documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the API documentation template to draft endpoint documentation for this route. Include purpose, parameters, response outcomes, and an example placeholder.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Code Comments
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these functions using the JSDoc and TSDoc guidance. Suggest comments only where they explain intent, contracts, errors, or non-obvious behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Design an AI-Ready Documentation Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the AI-friendly documentation guidance to plan a documentation set for agent consumption. Include llms.txt sections, core file references, key concepts, and RAG-friendly structure.

output_examples.input: A developer needs a README for a new command line tool.
An API team needs a standard page for a user lookup endpoint.
output_examples.output: A concise endpoint page with the route name, purpose, parameter table, response outcomes, and a request and response example placeholder.

output_examples.input: A team needs to document a database selection decision.

best_practices: Start with quick start steps and concrete examples before adding deeper reference material.
Adapt every template to the project so placeholders do not reach published documentation.
Keep AI-facing sections scoped, current, and self-contained for reliable retrieval.
anti_patterns: Copying templates without replacing placeholders or verifying project facts.
Adding comments that restate obvious implementation details line by line.
Publishing AI documentation with stale file maps or vague concept descriptions.

faq.question: What types of documentation does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers README files, API endpoint docs, code comments, changelogs, ADRs, llms.txt files, and AI-friendly structure guidance.

faq.question: Can it write complete documentation automatically?
faq.answer: It provides structure and templates. Complete documentation still needs accurate project details, examples, and review.

faq.question: Does it support API documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an endpoint template with purpose, parameters, response outcomes, and example placeholders.

faq.question: How does it help with AI-ready documentation?
faq.answer: It recommends clear hierarchy, self-contained sections, llms.txt content, file references, key concepts, and RAG-friendly organization.

faq.question: Is this skill tied to one programming language?
faq.answer: No. Most templates are language-neutral, with a small section for JSDoc and TSDoc comment structure.

faq.question: Does it require external tools?
faq.answer: No. The skill is a documentation guide and only declares read-oriented tools for inspecting files when context is needed.
